text.p: American adventurer Steve Fossett, seeking to become the first to circle the world nonstop in a balloon, entered Algerian airspace on Friday, an officer at the U.S. embassy in Rabat said.
"According to our latest information Fossett's balloon left Moroccan territory and entered Algerian airspace early this morning," the officer told Reuters.
He said: "At this stage we have no details on the exact position and speed of the balloon...What we know is that the balloon is continuing its way over Algeria."
MAP, quoting a national aeronautical source, earlier said that Fossett entered Moroccan airspace at 2250 GMT on Thursday between Tetouan in northern Morocco and the Spanish city of Malaga.
Just before midnight GMT he was seven miles north of al-Hoceima which lies on Morocco's Mediterranean coast, some 175 km (110 miles) west of the border with Algeria.
Moroccan civil aviation authorities said they had had no word from the 52-year-old balloonist who took off from St. Louis in the United States.
